programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc: Sometimes we get a bit stuck in the past with heritage homes, fixating on the original build year and forget that the home and society has evolved over 140 years. Subtle interventions were made during the heritage renovation, including the inclusion of a glass lift, but all was done to not only honour its past but also reflect how we live today.
programme.sub-title: Keeping the Heritage Alive in this 1880s Home Renovation

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Settled into an upper Sonoran site in North Scottsdale’s Whisper Rock Estates development, the Anderson residence embraces a design influenced by Territorial style of the mid-1800s, as well as later Southern California rambling ranch homes. Both movements are sympathetically reinterpreted to harmonize with the beauty of Whisper Rocks Estates and the Sonoran desert.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: At Mountainside, there was a natural flow of possibilities emanating from the desert itself. The powerful curves of the granite boulders dominated, yet they were held so gently by golden sands and delicate flora. Looking back, all of this spoke about balance and harmony, and this describes my clients as well.

programme.title: Australia ByDesign: Architecture
programme.desc: Uncovering the stories behind some of Australia ’s finest architectural design s, we visit Bruny Island’s house at the end of the world, shine a spotlight on renowned Victorian Government Architect, Jill Garner, and discover Lisa McGuigan’s bold cellar door vision in Vamp.

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Travel
programme.desc: In this episode, Ashley. Renne continues to explore sustainability in Thailand; She arrives in Koh Samui where she checks in to Tongsai Bay, the most sustainable hotel she's ever experienced, and she found them through the Green Pearls website.
programme.sub-title: Ep 2 - Most Eco-Friendly Resort In Thailand | Tongsai Bay

programme.title: Landscape Design
programme.desc: Onsite at the first project Landscape Fusion and Chibi Moku made the creative decision to take advantage of a major installation day on the active project in Seminole, FL to showcase the level of coordination and reliance on skilled craftsmanship that is essential to Landscape Fusion’s success as an outdoor living design/build company.
programme.sub-title: Behind the Landscape by Landscape Fusion | Tampa, Florida

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Fall is the perfect time to plan a full color landscape for spring. Let's face it, after a long winter we are starved for pops of color and bulb flowers are perfect. I show you how to quickly create a patch of color in your landscape in under 15 minutes.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: If you have pets or delicate plantings, it's essential to install deer fencing on your property to keep deer and other animals away. But most often, fence installers place these in unsightly locations. I wanted an alternative and devised a more robust post to allow for greater spans of netting, rendering the deer fencing on my property virtually invisible. Have a look to see how I did it.

programme.title: Australia ByDesign - Innovations
programme.desc: Our group of design industry experts have found some of the best and innovative design innovations from around Australia. In this episode, No Thru – the smartest fence ever, also from Melbourne a new technology for testing potential cures for neurological diseases using ‘mini brains’, Blade Stop – saving accidental cuts and amputations in the meat cutting industry, TM Checker – a new app from IP Australia for checking trademarks, and Paragon – an innovation that uses golden balls to intensify the taste of coffee.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: At The Greenwich House, Sabine created a custom barn door out of reclaimed wood from an old barn in Connecticut. It has quickly become a fan favorite within the home. Find out what it takes to get this look and create a custom reclaimed barn door for your own home.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Home design trends are always changing. But, what is the right choice for your home? Sabine meets with Mahdad Saniee, architect at The Greenwich House to learn about some of the design choices that created such a unique and highly livable home.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: This extraordinary, contemporary southwest home located behind the gates of the secluded community of Eagles Nest in Fountain Hills, Arizona is a luxurious, architectural-masterpiece, has 4 bedrooms, 6 bathroom home, with over 8,200 spacious square feet of custom features such as an elevator, air-conditioned garage with custom roll-up glass garage doors, an RV garage, fire and water features throughout, interior and exterior lit stairs and a custom, modern “cloud ceiling”.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Is your property ready for the winter? We have five tips for you to make sure your landscape and yard are healthy, strong, and ready for next season. programme.title: Australia ByDesign: Interiors

Then take a moment to watch this Desert Wash video and see modern living through a child's eye. It will change your perspective about what site-sensitive modern architecture can be.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Bold Backyards
programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. Traditionally you would pour a concrete footing and then stack the block; I wanted to see if it would work with rock and block adhesive. I love how it turned out, and it's doing amazing so far. If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc:
In this video, we'll show you shipping container homes and building examples from around the world and ask whether or not shipping container construction is the future?
The tiny house movement is growing rapidly and more container buildings are being constructed around the world, but is this the future of sustainable architecture? programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.
